title: Coarse-to-fine KV quantization sweep to trade GPU residency for quality
creator: Aisha Mehta
description: Run a systematic set of experiments that apply a coarse-to-fine quantization strategy to KV cache entries to reduce GPU working set while measuring downstream quality impact. The core idea: keep 'hot' KV entries at higher precision (FP8 or FP16 where available) and progressively quantize colder entries to INT8/INT4 with a small residual compensation layer and stochastic dequantization for sampling workloads. We want actionable thresholds for automatic per-entry fidelity demotion and a runtime policy to reclaim memory during bursts without violating quality SLOs.
hypothesis: We can reduce peak GPU KV residency by 35-60% on long-context workloads using tiered per-entry quantization with <2% relative degradation on generation quality (token-level logprob and end-to-end task metrics) for the bulk of traffic, and detect/mitigate outliers via fast fallback to full-precision entries.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Memory savings & latency: measured peak GPU KV memory reduction >= 30% on production-like trace and median p99 latency increase <= 10ms for generation requests.
2) Quality: aggregate token logprob drop <= 2% relative to baseline for 95% of traffic slices; targeted task metrics (QA EM / summarization ROUGE) drop <= 1.5% for high-value cohorts.
3) Safety: rollout policy with canary + automatic fallback kicks in when per-route quality regression exceeds thresholds; no permanent customer-facing errors during canary.
4) Observability: dashboards show per-cohort quality delta, demotion rates, and memory reclaimed; alerting on quality drift and demotion hot loops.
5) Playbook: runbook documented for reverting or tuning demotion thresholds and residual compensation parameters.
6) Implementation: runtime switch to enable/disable coarse-to-fine quantization with metrics gated behind telemetry flags.
7) Security/Compliance: no customer payload leaves host memory for quantization; KMS/HSM unaffected.
experiment_plan: A. Define three quantization tiers: HOT (FP8/FP16), WARM (INT8 with per-tile scale), COLD (INT4 block-packed + 8-bit residual buffer indexed per-1000 entries).
B. Implement per-entry telemetry: last_access_ts, access_count_decay, token_cohort (short/long/interactive), staleness_score. Use continuous batching hooks to mark hot entries during batch assembly.

C. Implement demotion policy: demote when staleness_score > 2x expected frequency and memory pressure > threshold. Promote synchronously on access miss to warm/hot with cheap upcast + refill streaming when available.

D. Residual compensation: store small 8-bit residuals for COLD-tier entries that reconstruct finer-grain vectors on read; fallback path to full-precision if reconstruction quality below route threshold.
E. A/B plan: Canary (5%), Ramp (20%), Full-scope (50%) with automatic rollback. Start on internal synthetic traces -> shadow production -> canary.

F. Metrics collection: token-level logprob delta, perplexity drift, EM/ROUGE for task slices, latency (p50/p95/p99), memory footprint per-GPU, demotion/promote counts, and reconstruction error distribution.
G. Long-tail detection: build a lightweight cohort detector that flags slices with >3x quality delta for immediate fallback and investigation.
H. Schedule: two-week implementation of runtime changes + one-week offline calibration on replay traces + two-week canary and analysis.
I. Safety nets: telemetry-gated revert, per-route opt-out, and per-customer whitelist to disable demotion.
J. Cost analysis: estimate theoretical token-cost savings from reduced memory pressure and improved packing (include expected GPU host-to-device transfer reduction during warmup-free workloads).
implementation_notes: Runtime hooks: add demotion incentive into KV lifecycle manager (C++ runtime) with bounded CPU overhead; prefer vectorized quant kernels on CUDA for INT8/INT4 encode/decode.

Batching integration: ensure demotion/promote occurs outside critical path for in-flight continuous batches; promotion should be asynchronous and return approximate vector quickly to avoid latency spikes.
Memory model: COLD entries stored block-packed in GPU global memory with per-block metadata; residuals stored in compressed stacked buffer that can be streamed back on demand.
Quant kernels: reuse existing tensor cores for FP8 and implement int4 packing using warp-level primitives; fallback to slower path for rare alignment cases.
Telemetry: add sampling in assembly stage to annotate batches with demotion state for downstream attribution in dashboards.
Testing: unit tests for encode/decode parity, integration tests with synthetic long-context traces, and end-to-end QA against eval suite (SQuAD, SummEval, synthetic hallucination tests).
infra_changes: Telemetry: new Prometheus counters + Grafana dashboards (kv.quant.demotion_rate, kv.quant.reconstruction_error_hist, kv.quant.memory_reclaimed)
CI: new nightly replay job to run calibration sweeps on recent traffic snapshot
Runtime flags: feature-flag gate and per-tenant opt-out stored in config service
Backfill storage: add compact index for residual buffer in GPU allocator metadata
results_summary: (placeholder) Initial offline replay indicates 38% median GPU KV memory reduction with ~0.9% average token logprob regression on long-context slices; however a small subset (~0.7%) of rare-cohort queries show >5% degradation, prompting implementation of a fast fallback path and tightened demotion thresholds for those cohorts.
rollout: Shadow-run against 10% production traffic for two weeks, then 5% canary for 72h with automated quality gates. If stable, ramp to 20% and hold for one week before wider rollout. All ramps controlled by feature flag and per-route rollouts in console.
risks: Long-tail quality regressions that are hard to detect without thorough cohorting
Promotion latency spikes causing tail-latency regressions if async refill congestion occurs
Quantization-induced distribution shifts that affect downstream rerankers or cached prompt templates
Complexity in allocator metadata increases GC risk under high churn
next_steps: Complete C++ runtime implementation and land PR #1842
Run offline calibration sweeps on last 7 days of traffic and refine demotion thresholds
Add cohort detector and per-route opt-out in console
Start shadow-run and publish initial dashboard to SRE/PM/Applied ML for review
Draft runbook for rollback and threshold tuning
